_why: `_cmd_alive`'s cmux arm matched with `cmux tree --all | grep -q`. Under the wrapper's global pipefail that reports a MATCH as 141 -- grep -q exits at the first hit, the producer takes SIGPIPE -- so a LIVE agent reads as dead, the dangerous direction for an aliveness predicate. Measured 2026-09-01 with a bulk-writing stub: 240 KB tree with the target on line 1 -> rc 141; the same tree at 110 B -> rc 0.
_scope_note: The pipe buffer is NOT the real bound here. Unlike the `printf` sites, this producer is an external process, so a `tree` that streams its output can be SIGPIPEd at any size -- measured: an incrementally-writing stub inverted at 110 B. Any size-based rule-out of an external-producer pipeline is therefore unsound.
_provenance: Third site of the class found by the 282a3a5 sweep's re-examination, after the recovered-response predicate (agy_recovery_sigpipe.json). The original sweep ruled this site out as 'operational surface tree rather than retained terminal content' -- a reachability argument that was never measured.

mutations.name: cmux-alive-uses-pipe
mutations._mechanism: Restore the pipeline. A tree past the pipe buffer that DOES contain the surface then reports 141, and `alive` declares a live agent dead.
